newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Telekom sell-off adviser accord signed.
newsitem.headline: Turk Telekom sell-off adviser accord signed.

text.p: Turkey's Privatisation Administration (OIB) and a consortium headed by Goldman Sachs on Friday signed an adviser agreement for the sale of state telecommunications company Turk Telekom.
The office of State Minister Ufuk Soylemez said in a statement that with the signing of the accord it will be possible to offer a first tranche of Turk Telekom shares in 1997.
The government plans to sell around 10-15 percent of the company in the first tranche.

The consortium which Goldman Sachs heads will begin work immediately on assessing the value of Turk Telekom shares. It will also look into reform in the sector and producing accounts in line with international standards, the statement said.
It said the signing of the accord in Ankara followed long talks coordinated with the World Bank on the sale of Turk Telekom, the centrepiece of Turkey's sell-off programme.
Earlier this year Turkey's constitutional court gave the green light for the sell-off, after having blocked it three times since 1993.
The court ruled in favour of a law which allows for the sale of 49 percent of Turk Telekom's shares.
Under the law, a 34 percent stake is planned to be sold to domestic or foreign investors, 10 percent to the country's postal services and five percent to Turk Telekom employees.
